No blocking findings. This verdict supersedes — without erasing — the earlier premature 338-message ACCEPT, which the parent correctly held as not accepted pending these exact reads.

### What the correction does, independently re-verified

The single authorized change is `src/core/helper-refs.ts:150-152`: inside `shortSessionRef`'s reversed-alias loop, `if (peers.some((peer) => peer.startsWith(alias))) continue;` precedes `uniqueSessionPrefix`. Traced against the recorded rejection case (Pi `route-hit` + OMP `~sk1_…["omp","route-hit"]`): the OMP row's native alias is whole-shadowed by the Pi peer's identical alias; `uniqueSessionPrefix` filters equal peers (`peer !== self`), so without the guard the 8-char `route-hi` escaped as "unique" and stage-3 route-prefix resolution bound it to the Pi row. The guard closes exactly that: any alias that is a prefix of (or equal to) another session's alias yields no safe candidate prefix, so it is skipped and `stableSessionRef` falls back to the full route id — matching the recorded corrected outcomes (collision row prints the full encoded route; `Ordinary UUID` still prints `01a07264`; shared-UUID rows print unshared native prefixes `2026-09-05`/`2026-09-06`; `shadowed-long` prints `shadowed-`). One short-circuit scan per alias; no new resolver invocations, maps, or candidate allocations. Resolver stages/exactOnly, `uniqueSessionPrefix`, CLI `decodeRouteId`/`sessionHarnessId` missing-native inference, and `parseRef` error policy are provably untouched. Guard present identically at lib/helper-refs.js:180, public/app.js:404, public/browser.js:5830, public/helpers.js:1030, skills/lib/pi-dish-client.js:148.
